items.q: Choose the word closest in meaning to CANDID.
items.x: Candid means honest and direct.

items.q: Choose the word closest in meaning to METICULOUS.
items.x: Meticulous means very careful about detail.

items.q: Choose the word closest in meaning to CLANDESTINE.
items.x: Clandestine means done secretly.

items.q: Choose the word closest in meaning to MITIGATE.
items.x: To mitigate is to make less severe.

items.q: Choose the word closest in meaning to PRUDENT.
items.x: Prudent means sensible and careful.

items.q: Choose the word closest in meaning to VOLATILE.
items.x: Volatile means liable to change suddenly.

items.q: Choose the word closest in meaning to INSURGENT.
items.x: An insurgent rises against authority.

items.q: Choose the word closest in meaning to CORROBORATE.
items.x: To corroborate is to support with evidence.

items.q: Choose the word OPPOSITE in meaning to SCARCE.
items.x: Scarce means in short supply.

items.q: Choose the word OPPOSITE in meaning to HOSTILE.
items.x: Hostile means unfriendly or aggressive.

items.q: Choose the word OPPOSITE in meaning to TRANSPARENT.
items.x: Opaque means not see-through, or not open.

items.q: Choose the word OPPOSITE in meaning to ESCALATE.
items.x: To escalate is to intensify.

items.q: Choose the word OPPOSITE in meaning to LOYAL.
items.x: Treacherous means betraying trust.

items.q: Choose the word OPPOSITE in meaning to CONCEAL.
items.x: To conceal is to hide.

items.q: “To bury the hatchet” means to…
items.x: To end a quarrel.

items.q: “To let the cat out of the bag” means to…
items.x: To disclose something secret by mistake.

items.q: “A blessing in disguise” is…
o: Something good that first seemed bad
items.x: An apparent misfortune that turns out well.

items.q: “To burn the midnight oil” means to…
items.x: To work or study late.

items.q: “To be on the fence” means to be…
items.x: Not yet choosing a side.

items.q: “To read between the lines” means to…
items.x: To understand what is implied but not stated.

items.q: Neither the minister nor his aides ___ present.
items.x: With neither/nor the verb agrees with the nearer subject, “aides” (plural).

items.q: Each of the officers ___ a weapon.
items.x: “Each” is singular.

items.q: The committee ___ reached its decision.
items.x: The committee acting as one body takes a singular verb, matching “its”.

items.q: News of the attacks ___ spreading quickly.
items.x: “News” is singular.

items.q: One of the suspects ___ escaped.
items.x: The subject is “one”, which is singular.

items.q: Bread and butter ___ his usual breakfast.
items.x: Treated as a single dish, it takes a singular verb.

items.q: Choose the correct sentence.
o: He is more senior than me.
items.x: “Senior” takes “to”.

items.q: Choose the correct sentence.
o: I am looking forward to meet you.
I am looking forward to meeting you.
I am looking forward for meeting you.
items.x: “Look forward to” is followed by the -ing form.

items.q: Choose the correct sentence.
items.x: “Information” is uncountable and singular.

items.q: Choose the correct sentence.
items.x: “Discuss” takes a direct object, no preposition.

items.q: Choose the correct sentence.
o: Between you and I, it failed.
Between you and me, it failed.
Between you and myself, it failed.
Among you and me, it failed.
items.x: After a preposition use the object pronoun “me”.

items.q: Choose the correct sentence.
o: He has been working here since five years.
He has been working here for five years.
He is working here since five years.
He works here for five years.
items.x: Use “for” with a period of time, “since” with a starting point.

items.passage: The Lake Chad basin, shared by Nigeria, Niger, Chad and Cameroon, has shrunk dramatically since the 1960s because of drought, rising demand for water and poor management. As fishing and farming collapsed, many young people lost their livelihoods. Armed groups have exploited this, offering money and a sense of purpose. Experts argue that military action alone cannot end the insurgency; restoring the lake's economy and providing jobs are just as important.
items.q: According to the passage, why have armed groups found recruits?
o: Because young people lost their livelihoods
items.x: The passage links lost livelihoods to recruitment.

items.passage: The Lake Chad basin, shared by Nigeria, Niger, Chad and Cameroon, has shrunk dramatically since the 1960s because of drought, rising demand for water and poor management. items.q: What do the experts in the passage recommend?
o: Moving people away from the lake
items.x: They say military action alone is not enough.

items.q: The word “exploited” in the passage most nearly means…
items.x: To exploit a situation is to take advantage of it.

items.passage: Open-source intelligence has grown in importance because so much information is now public. Satellite images, social media posts and shipping data can reveal troop movements or smuggling routes. However, analysts must verify what they find, since false information spreads quickly and can be planted deliberately.
items.q: What is the main caution the passage gives?
items.x: False information can spread or be planted, so verify.

items.passage: Open-source intelligence has grown in importance because so much information is now public. Satellite images, social media posts and shipping data can reveal troop movements or smuggling routes. However, analysts must verify what they find, since false information spreads quickly and can be planted deliberately.
items.q: Which is given as an example of open-source information?
items.x: Shipping data is publicly available.

items.q: All analysts are officers. Some officers are linguists. Which must be true?
o: No conclusion about analysts and linguists is certain
items.x: The linguists might not include any analysts.

items.q: If it rains, the match is cancelled. The match was not cancelled. Therefore…
items.x: If rain always cancels the match, no cancellation means no rain.

items.q: Doctor is to hospital as teacher is to…
items.x: The place where each works.

items.q: Which word does not belong? Abuja, Lagos, Niamey, Accra
items.x: The others are capital cities.

items.q: Ade is taller than Bisi. Bisi is taller than Chidi. Who is shortest?
items.x: Ade > Bisi > Chidi.

items.q: Which comes next? A, C, F, J, O, …
items.x: Gaps grow by one: +2, +3, +4, +5, +6 → U.

items.q: Some spies are diplomats. All diplomats speak French. Which must be true?
items.x: The spies who are diplomats speak French.

items.q: Which word does not belong? Mali, Niger, Burkina Faso, Ghana
items.x: Ghana is still in ECOWAS; the others formed the AES.
